meanings.note: Leave a person without support.
Give up a plan or activity.
Stop an activity or bring something to a halt.
Quit doing something.

examples.text: Il arrête de travailler à six heures.
Sans toi, je crois que j'arrêterais ce métier.
examples.trans: Without you, I think I'd quit this job.

meanings.note: Moi aussi = me too. Invariable French adverb meaning 'also'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.

examples.text: Tu déjeunes aussi avec Dany Boon.
examples.trans: You're also having lunch with Dany Boon.

examples.text: Tu déjeunes aussi avec Dany Boon demain.
examples.trans: You're also having lunch with Dany Boon tomorrow.

meanings.note: as an interjection: bon, alors... = right, so...
as an interjection: bon, alors... = right, so...

meanings.en: bonne journée = have a nice day
meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'good'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.
Silly or foolish; can be affectionate in a friendly exchange.

meanings.en: une bête = an animal, a beast (noun)
meanings.note: As a feminine noun, une bête is an animal.

examples.text: Ce sont juste des bêtes de foire.

meanings.note: determiner: ce soir = tonight, cette semaine = this week
pronoun: c'est = it is; tout ce que = all that

examples.text: Je ne peux pas venir ce soir.
Cette agence ne représente que des stars.
Magali, je dois voir la pièce de Koltès cette semaine.
examples.trans: Magali, I have to see the Koltès play this week.

meanings.note: Believe that something is true.
Think or suppose, often softening an opinion.
D' before a vowel. Core French preposition meaning 'of', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.
le film de Tarantino = Tarantino's film
Also 'some': du sucre. Core French preposition meaning 'of', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.
je suis désolé(e) = I'm sorry; désolé! alone also works
Take a person or animal along to another place. For carrying an object away, use emporter.

examples.text: Elle emmène son fils à l'école.
examples.trans: She takes her son to school.

examples.text: Quand tu voudras un enfant, je t'emmènerai en Hollande.
examples.trans: When you want a child, I'll take you to Holland.

meanings.note: en retard = late, en vacances = on holiday

examples.text: Oh non! Je suis en retard.

meanings.note: Un enfant for a boy or child of unspecified gender; une enfant for a girl.

examples.text: Je voulais un enfant, et pas elle.
examples.trans: I wanted a child, and she didn't.

meanings.note: Exceptional creative or intellectual ability; une idée de génie, a brilliant idea.

meanings.en: une idée de génie = a stroke of genius
meanings.note: A person with exceptional ability; the noun remains masculine.

examples.trans: It was a stroke of genius.

examples.text: Line Renaud, c'était une idée de génie.
examples.trans: Line Renaud was a stroke of genius.

meanings.note: The day before today; hier soir means last night.

examples.trans: I'd like to apologise for yesterday.

examples.text: On a fait quoi hier soir?
examples.trans: What did we do last night?

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la idée', plural 'les idées') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'idea'.

examples.text: Paris? C'est une très bonne idée.
examples.trans: Paris? That's a very good idea.

meanings.note: J' before a vowel. High-frequency French pronoun meaning 'I'; clitic object forms precede the conjugated verb.

examples.text: Gabriel! Je suis à mon cours d'équitation.
examples.trans: Gabriel! I'm at my horse-riding lesson.

meanings.note: merci beaucoup = thank you very much

examples.text: Merci beaucoup pour votre aide précieuse aujourd'hui.
examples.trans: Thank you very much for your valuable help today.

examples.text: Je te dis mille fois merci pour ce beau rôle!
examples.trans: I thank you a thousand times for this great role!

meanings.note: Stressed form: pour moi, avec moi. High-frequency French pronoun meaning 'me'; clitic object forms precede the conjugated verb.

examples.text: C'est comme un rêve pour moi.
examples.trans: It's like a dream for me.

meanings.note: A job, trade or profession.

examples.trans: What do you do for a living?

examples.text: Sans toi, je crois que j'arrêterais ce métier.
examples.trans: Without you, I think I'd quit this job.

meanings.note: ne... pas = not; ne... rien = nothing; ne... que = only; n' before a vowel

examples.text: Tarantino ne prendra pas Cécile. Problème d'âge.
examples.trans: Tarantino won't take Cécile. A problem with her age.

meanings.note: Surprise or dismay. Spoken French interj expression meaning 'oh', common in natural conversation.

examples.text: Oh non! Je suis en retard.

meanings.note: Invariable French adverb meaning 'yes'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.

examples.text: Oui, oui. J'ai juste besoin d'un petit cours.
examples.trans: Yes, yes. I just need a little lesson.

meanings.note: second half of ne... pas; in speech ne is often dropped

examples.text: Tarantino ne prendra pas Cécile. Problème d'âge.
examples.trans: Tarantino won't take Cécile. A problem with her age.

meanings.note: before an infinitive: pour faire plaisir

examples.text: Je suis là pour voir Mathias.

examples.trans: It's like a dream for me.

meanings.note: Question word or conjunction. Invariable French adverb meaning 'when'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.

examples.text: Dis-lui que je ne peux pas venir.
Appelle Clémentine. Dis-lui que je ne peux pas venir ce soir.
examples.trans: Call Clémentine. Tell her I can't come tonight.

meanings.note: Without a person, thing or action.

examples.text: Sans rendez-vous? Je ne promets rien.
examples.trans: Without an appointment? I'm not promising anything.

meanings.note: Bonne soirée = have a nice evening. Feminine noun ('la soirée', plural 'les soirées') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'evening'.

examples.trans: Two tickets for Tuesday? On Tuesday you've got the Kechiche film.

meanings.note: indefinite article; des in the plural
Number; l'un = one of them. Spoken French det expression meaning 'a', common in natural conversation.

examples.text: L'un à midi, l'autre à deux heures.
examples.trans: One at noon, the other at two.

meanings.note: + noun or infinitive. French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire'). Core French verb meaning 'to want'.
